newsitem.title: HONDURAS: Honduran army ordered to seize ballot boxes.
newsitem.headline: Honduran army ordered to seize ballot boxes.

text.p: The National Electoral Tribunal of Honduras on Tuesday ordered the Honduran army to seize ballot boxes and electoral documents from groups that have alleged fraud from Sunday's primary election.
In 17 of the 18 departments (provinces) of this Central American country, dissident activists from both of the major parties have held on to ballot boxes, alleging fraud.

During Sunday's primary elections, the ruling Liberal Party chose Congressman Carlos Flores as its candidate for November 1997 presidential elections, while the opposition National Party chose teacher Nora Gunera, the widow of a former military strongman who ran Honduras in the 1970s.
"The tribunal in full ordered the armed forces to seize all of the electoral material in possession of the local commissions," the president of the tribunal, Mario Aguilar, told reporters.

Most of the ballot boxes were being held by dissidents of the National Party who are challenging Gunera's victory, claiming their presidential candidate should be Elias Asfura, the second-place finisher.

Renan Inestroza, secretary general of the Avance movement, which supports Asfura, called on followers "not to allow ballot boxes and election materials to be transferred to the capital because we don't have confidence in the National Electoral Tribunal."
